reviewMetrics.metricCaveat: This audit measures whether the five existing country-level prose fields can be defended. It does not measure the completeness of DRC cultural documentation.

currentFields.finding: The current sentence combines distinct Luba, Lunda, and Chokwe artistic traditions with Congolese rumba and several unsourced nationwide craft categories.

supportedClaims.claim: Luba and Lunda courtly arts developed within specific political and historical settings in the southern Central African savanna.
Chokwe court art includes carved prestige objects associated with chiefly authority, ritual, and historical memory.
Congolese rumba is a shared urban musical and dance tradition of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo, inscribed by UNESCO in 2021.

removeOrRelocate: Remove generic references to traditional dance, basketry, pottery, weaving, and traditional architecture unless each is tied to a named community, region, practice, and source.
Relocate people-specific artistic and ritual traditions to people fiches or thematic dossiers, retaining only a short sourced country overview.

currentFields.finding: The phrase 'Catholic majority' is not supported by the 2013–2014 DHS respondent distribution. The same survey records several Christian categories, while later external estimates use different classifications.

supportedClaims.claim: In the 2013–2014 DHS sample of women and men aged 15–49, Christian affiliations predominated, but respondents were distributed among Catholic, Protestant, Kimbanguist, Salvation Army, and other Christian categories; Muslim, animist, unaffiliated, and other responses were also recorded.
Religious-demography estimates vary by source, and some people combine traditional practices with Christian or other affiliations.

limitations: The DHS table describes surveyed women and men in specified age ranges, not a full-population census.
The U.S. State Department report cites third-party estimates and should be used as contextual synthesis, not as the sole denominator.
Do not collapse Kimbanguist and other locally rooted Christian affiliations into an undefined 'traditional beliefs' bucket.

currentFields.finding: The current field presents rural life, farming, livestock, fishing, mining, and trade as one national lifestyle. These are economic activities with strong regional, urban-rural, gender, and conflict-related variation.

supportedClaims.claim: Agricultural livelihoods and food security conditions vary substantially by region and are affected by conflict, displacement, markets, and climate shocks.
The extractive sector has a major role in the national economy, but aggregate export and revenue indicators do not describe the everyday livelihood of the population as a whole.

removeOrRelocate: Remove 'mainly rural' unless it is tied to a current, dated urbanization measure.
Move crop, livestock, fishing, mining, and trade descriptions into region- or livelihood-specific modules with separate sources.
Do not infer household livelihoods from national GDP, export, or government-revenue shares.

currentFields.finding: The current sentence asserts one system of chiefdoms, clans, descent, extended families, lineages, ancestors, and elder councils across a highly diverse country. The parenthetical acknowledgement of patrilineal or matrilineal variation does not make the generalization auditable.
removeOrRelocate: Remove the current country-level sentence from validated display.
Document descent, authority, kinship, and council systems in individual people fiches or comparative thematic dossiers.
Require a named community, place, observation period, and scholarly source for every replacement claim.

currentFields.finding: Listing every neighbouring country does not document a historical relation, and the statement that the diaspora is important in Belgium, France, and Western countries has no dated bilateral dataset attached.

supportedClaims.claim: The UN International Migrant Stock 2024 dataset provides a reproducible basis for measuring migrants of DRC origin and their destinations.

removeOrRelocate: Replace generic neighbour-country relations with typed, dated, and sourced relation records between named peoples or political entities.
Do not identify Belgium, France, or any other country as a leading destination until the origin-destination matrix has been extracted and recorded with its reference year.
Keep migration-stock estimates distinct from ancestry, citizenship, refugee, and self-identified diaspora measures.

proposedSources.title: Congolese rumba
proposedSources.scope: urban musical and dance practice shared by the two Congo states
proposedSources.caveat: UNESCO inscription does not make rumba representative of every community, region, or musical tradition in the DRC.

proposedSources.title: Kingdoms of the Savanna: The Luba and Lunda Empires
proposedSources.publisher: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History
proposedSources.scope: Luba and Lunda political and artistic practices

proposedSources.title: Mwanangana (lord of the land) playing a sanza
proposedSources.scope: one documented example of Chokwe court art
proposedSources.caveat: An object record supports a scoped example, not a complete summary of Chokwe art across time and territory.

proposedSources.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo Demographic and Health Survey 2013–2014
proposedSources.publisher: DRC Ministry of Planning, DRC Ministry of Public Health, and ICF International
proposedSources.scope: surveyed respondent characteristics, including declared religious affiliation
proposedSources.caveat: The relevant table covers surveyed women and men in specified age ranges and must not be presented as a full-population religious census.

proposedSources.title: 2023 Report on International Religious Freedom: Democratic Republic of the Congo
proposedSources.scope: religious diversity, legal context, and comparison of third-party estimates
proposedSources.caveat: Population shares in this report are attributed to external datasets with different reference years and classifications.

proposedSources.title: GIEWS Country Brief: Democratic Republic of the Congo
proposedSources.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
proposedSources.scope: current agricultural production and food-security context
proposedSources.caveat: This time-sensitive brief focuses on food security and conflict effects; it is not a general ethnography or exhaustive livelihood survey.

proposedSources.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo
proposedSources.caveat: National economic contribution does not establish how many people depend on mining or describe household lifestyles.

proposedSources.title: International Migrant Stock 2024
proposedSources.publisher: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
proposedSources.scope: international migrant stock by origin and destination
proposedSources.caveat: Migrant stock is not equivalent to citizenship, ancestry, refugee status, or self-identified diaspora. Bilateral destination claims require extraction from the origin-destination table.

doNotInfer: Do not treat one named tradition as representative of every DRC community.
Do not call Catholicism a population majority from the available DHS respondent table.
Do not describe national lifestyles from lists of economic sectors.
Do not assign one kinship or authority system to the whole country.
Do not equate neighbouring states with documented historical relations.
Do not equate migrant stock with the full diaspora.

remainingResearch: Select representative people- and region-specific cultural dossiers instead of expanding one national traditions list.
Decide whether the public country surface should show dated survey distributions or a qualitative religious-diversity summary.
Create region- or livelihood-specific modules for agriculture, fishing, pastoralism, urban work, trade, and mining where accepted sources exist.
Move kinship, descent, chiefly authority, and council descriptions into people fiches with scholarly references.
Extract the DRC origin-destination matrix from UN DESA International Migrant Stock 2024 before naming leading diaspora destinations.
Create typed cross-border relation records for named peoples and political entities.
